claim.text:
This paper presents a bounded, guard-first evaluation of adaptive virtual
inertia and damping coordination by multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL)
in four paralleled virtual synchronous generators (VSGs). On the sealed
corrected-60-Hz benchmark, 121 of 208 all-fresh policies met both aggregate
decoupling endpoints, but none met the profile-complete
endpoint-plus-command-activity contract. The evaluation first fixes an
exactly-once device-to-system-base conversion, physical 60-Hz observation
semantics, common--differential response-energy endpoints, and a deterministic
direct-$M/D$ comparator. It then crosses authentic and row-permuted actor
source, critic source, and reward access with 26 matched seeds and a fixed
43,200-step budget. All 832 policy--profile blocks exceeded both registered
comparator-relative normalized command-RMS and command-total-variation limits;
397 also failed the rate-of-change-of-frequency guard and 37 failed the
worst-frequency-peak guard. No registered 6-s or separate 30-s source contrast
established its positive 10\% material effect after Holm control. The direct
$M/D$ comparator separately passed 4/4 fresh profiles at 30 s. These results
separate endpoint improvement from complete qualification for one finite
benchmark; the command metrics are activity summaries rather than physical
safety or hardware-harm measures.

claim.text:
Adaptive inertia and damping can improve an aggregate decoupling score without
qualifying a controller for coordinated operation. In one illustrative R485
policy, arm \texttt{an\_cn\_r0} with training seed 501 attained aggregate
off-diagonal and disturbance-differential response-energy ratios of 0.535918
and 0.905632 relative to the deterministic comparator, so both endpoints
improved by more than the registered 5\%. Nevertheless, all four profile
guards failed, including both command-activity checks on every profile. This
example is not a selected success or failure case: it makes concrete the
population-level result that 121 of 208 all-fresh policies met both aggregate
endpoints whereas 0 of 208 met the complete contract. The distinction matters
for paralleled VSGs because inertia-like fleet support and differential motion
between units are different control objectives. VSG and parallel-VSM studies
have established the importance of inertia, damping, electrical coupling, and
inter-unit coordination~\cite{zhong2011synchronverters,darco2013vsm,
wu2016smallsignal,gonzalez2022parallel}; the present question is how a learned
adaptive controller should be qualified when these objectives and its command
path disagree.

claim.text:
We ask the following bounded question: under an exactly-once
device-to-system-base conversion on a 60-Hz plant, does any all-fresh policy
from the registered $M/D$-adaptive MARL family satisfy both decoupling
endpoints and every profile-level guard relative to a deterministic direct-$M/D$
comparator? The hard constraints are part of the question. Policies are
evaluated at their final checkpoint after a fixed 43,200-step budget; the four
benchmark profiles are outcome-visible frozen records rather than a population
sample; a policy qualifies only if both equal-weight aggregate endpoints
improve by at least 5\% and all four profiles satisfy trajectory, frequency,
saturation, dispersion, and comparator-relative normalized command-RMS and
command-total-variation guards. The 6-s primary and 30-s tail analyses are
derived from the same traces and remain separate. The command metrics quantify
relative command activity, not actuator energy, wear, hardware harm, or
physical safety.

claim.text:
Three challenges prevent a direct reuse of conventional learned-controller
reporting. The first is semantic comparability: controller arithmetic is
defined on the device base, the simulator stores $M/D$ on the system base, and
the 60-Hz physical endpoints must not receive a second conversion. The second
is qualification: aggregate endpoint improvement and profile-level contract
compliance are different logical decisions, and pooling profiles or horizons
can hide their disagreement. The third is source attribution: stochastic
training variation can dominate actor-, critic-, or reward-source differences,
while a source replacement can change more than semantic neighbour information.
Each challenge therefore requires a distinct part of the evaluation rather
than a stronger claim from the same summary metric.

claim.text:
The evaluation addresses these challenges in one-to-one form.
Section~\ref{sec:contract} defines the corrected parameter, action, coordinate,
endpoint, and deterministic-comparator contract, with the 60-Hz transform
applied exactly once. Section~\ref{sec:protocol} then separates endpoint
calculation from a profile-complete guard decision and reports 6-s and 30-s
results without pooling; the development-selected direct-$M/D$ controller is
evaluated on a separate prospectively fresh bank. The same section crosses
authentic and row-permuted actor source, critic source, and reward access in a
$2\times2\times2$ design with 26 matched training seeds. Registered seed-level
contrasts, a 10\% materiality boundary, and Holm control make the source
question distinct from policy qualification. Together, these elements
evaluate the MARL controller as an object under test rather than present it as
a qualified solution.

claim.text:
The contributions are threefold. First, Section~\ref{sec:contract} formulates
the qualification problem through a corrected semantic contract that binds
device/system-base conversion, 60-Hz coordinates, endpoints, and
comparator-relative command activity to one profile-complete decision. Second,
Section~\ref{sec:protocol} gives a prospective guard-first evaluation design
with separate deterministic and learned-policy banks, a fixed final-checkpoint
budget, and non-pooled 6-s and 30-s horizons. Third,
Section~\ref{sec:results} reports the bounded R485 empirical finding from the
matched paired-seed source factorial: 121/208 policies met both aggregate
endpoints, 5/208 also met every non-command guard in a post-hoc Pareto read,
but 0/208 met the complete contract; no registered source contrast established
its positive material effect after Holm control, whereas the direct-$M/D$
comparator separately passed 4/4 fresh profiles. These are finite-benchmark
qualification results, not a universal verdict on MARL.

claim.text:
At each $\Delta t=\SI{0.2}{s}$ control instant, controller $i$ produces a
two-component normalized target $\bar a_i$. With componentwise
$\Pi_c(x)=\min\{c,\max\{-c,x\}\}$ and $a_i^{\rm exec}[-1]=0$, the common
projection is
\begin{align}
a_i^{\rm amp}[k]&=\Pi_1(\bar a_i[k]),\nonumber\\
a_i^{\rm exec}[k]&=\Pi_1\!\left(a_i^{\rm exec}[k-1]\right.\nonumber\\
&\quad\left.+\Pi_{0.25}\!\left(a_i^{\rm amp}[k]
-a_i^{\rm exec}[k-1]\right)\right).
\label{eq:projection}
\end{align}
For either component, $q(a)=600a$ when $a\geq0$ and $q(a)=200a$ otherwise.
The device-base commands are
\begin{align}
M_i^{\rm dev}[k]&=\max\{20,M_{i,0}^{\rm dev}+q(a_i^{M,{\rm exec}}[k])\},\nonumber\\
D_i^{\rm dev}[k]&=\max\{10,D_{i,0}^{\rm dev}+q(a_i^{D,{\rm exec}}[k])\}.
\label{eq:action_map}
\end{align}
After~\eqref{eq:base_conversion}, targets are linearly applied over five
simulator substeps from the preceding runtime readback. Projection precedes
decoding; the learned command does not directly inject active power.

claim.text:
Each profile contains positive and negative common, differential, and localized
load probes. A learned-policy block must be valid, preserve the registered
mapping, bound and slew invariants, keep saturation fraction at most 0.05, and
meet nondegeneracy and per-VSG dispersion floors of $10^{-6}$. Common-frequency
integral, worst-frequency peak, and RoCoF must be no worse than 1.03 times the
same-profile direct-$M/D$ values. Comparator-relative normalized command RMS
and total variation (TV) must each be no worse than 1.10 times the comparator.

A policy meets the complete contract only when all four benchmark profiles
meet every block-level guard and the equal-weight aggregate ratios of both
$J_{\rm cross}$ and $J_d$ to direct $M/D$ are at most 0.95. The endpoint and
guard decisions are therefore conjunctive. The frequency and command
multipliers are registered empirical tolerances. In particular, normalized
command RMS and TV do not contain a calibrated actuator transfer, damage
functional, hardware limit, or safety certificate.

claim.text:
For a profile with common/differential magnitude $q$ and localized magnitude
$\ell$, the common probe applies $\pm q/4$ to each of four loads; the
differential probe applies $\pm q/4$ to the two area-1 loads and $\mp q/4$ to
the two area-2 loads; the localized probe applies $\pm\ell$ at its named load.
Each profile therefore contributes six signed scenarios. The 14 exact
profile cards, including baseline $M/D$, steady loads, magnitudes, and localized
load, are fixed in the sealed R481 and R485 contracts; no result was used to
change them.

The deterministic family contains zero command and nine local-neighbour laws
with $(k_M,k_D)\in\{0.5,1,2\}^2$. For ring-neighbour set $\mathcal N_i$, define
$\phi_i=2\pi60(\omega_i-1)/3$, $\rho_i=2\pi60\dot\omega_i/5$, and
$\sigma_i=|\phi_i|+|\rho_i|$. Before~\eqref{eq:projection}, the law forms
\begin{align}
\bar a_i^M&=\tanh\!\left[k_M\!\left(\sigma_i-
\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal N_i}\sigma_j\right)\right],\nonumber\\
\bar a_i^D&=\tanh\!\left[k_D\!\left(|\phi_i|+
\frac12\sum_{j\in\mathcal N_i}(|\phi_i-\phi_j|+|\rho_i-\rho_j|)\right)\right].
\label{eq:direct_md}
\end{align}
A frozen lexicographic development rule selected $(k_M,k_D)=(2,2)$; the law
was not reselected in R485.

claim.text:
The learner comprises four independent per-VSG soft actor--critic
agents~\cite{haarnoja2018sac}. Each agent uses a seven-component canonical physical
observation: local active power, local frequency and RoCoF, and the frequency
and RoCoF of its two ring neighbours. Appending the previously executed
two-component command gives a nine-dimensional Markov state. A Gaussian--tanh
actor and twin-Q critic each use four 128-unit ReLU hidden layers. Adam has
learning rate $3\times10^{-4}$; $\gamma=0.99$, target rate $\tau=0.005$,
replay capacity 10,000, batch size 256, target entropy $-2$, entropy coefficient
bounds $[0.005,5]$, and gradient-norm clipping at one. Training is stochastic;
evaluation uses the deterministic actor mean.

All six learner frequency/RoCoF slots use one canonical $60/50$ transform.
Actor, critic, replay, reward, and evaluation consume the transformed rows; no
path applies it twice. Authentic source $N$ preserves the same-time neighbour
tuple. Placebo source $P$ preserves recipient-local slots but takes the four
neighbour slots from row $\pi(i)=(i+1)\bmod4$. The $N/P$ contrast is therefore
a total input-source intervention, not an isolated semantic-information
intervention.

claim.text:
The per-agent reward is
\begin{equation}
r_i=100r_{f,i}+50r_{{\rm abs},i}+0.0056r_H+0.0056r_D,
\label{eq:reward}
\end{equation}
where reward access toggles only the registered neighbour-frequency terms.
$r_H$ and $r_D$ penalize squared fleet-mean $M$ and $D$ commands normalized by
600. The reward has no command-TV term and is never used by the evaluation
contract. The design crosses actor source $\{N,P\}$, critic source $\{N,P\}$,
and reward access $\{0,1\}$ with matched seeds 501--526. All 208 cells were
newly trained for exactly 43,200 interaction steps. Only the final checkpoint
enters qualification and source inference; no R483/R484 checkpoint, replay,
curve, or result row entered R485.

Each final policy ran once on the four benchmark profiles for 150 steps at
$\Delta t=\SI{0.2}{s}$. The first 30 steps produce the registered 6-s primary
prefix of the same 30-s trace. The two horizons share policies, seeds, and
trajectories, so they are reported separately and are not independent
replications.

claim.text:
Let $y_{acrps}=\log L_{acrps}$, where $L$ is the positive final-checkpoint
$J_d$ for actor source $a$, critic source $c$, reward access $r$, profile $p$,
and seed $s$. Equal-weight averaging over nuisance indices gives the four
registered within-seed contrasts
\begin{align}
d_s^A&=\langle y_{Pcrps}-y_{Ncrps}\rangle_{c,r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^C&=\langle y_{aPrps}-y_{aNrps}\rangle_{a,r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^{AC}&=\langle y_{PNrps}-y_{NNrps}-y_{PPrps}+y_{NPrps}\rangle_{r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^{CR}&=\langle y_{aP1ps}-y_{aN1ps}-y_{aP0ps}+y_{aN0ps}\rangle_{a,p}.
\label{eq:contrasts}
\end{align}
Positive main effects indicate lower loss with authentic $N$; interaction signs
retain the registered ratio-of-ratios meaning. The 26 seeds, not profiles or
trajectories, are inference units. Exact one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests
compare each Hodges--Lehmann location to $\log(1.10)$, with one Holm family of
four~\cite{holm1979simple}. Non-rejection is neither zero effect nor
equivalence.

The formal inventory verifies 1,082/1,082 terminal artifacts and
5,088/5,088 trajectories, with no missing, duplicate, hash-invalid, or
parse-invalid item. All 848 6-s summaries are derived prefixes; no
available-case analysis or horizon pooling was performed.

claim.text:
The central result is a qualification reversal, not an absence of useful
endpoint motion: endpoint-only assessment admits 121 policies, while the
registered complete contract admits none. The deterministic result separately
shows that the corrected comparator object has a nonempty finite fresh-bank
feasible set. Neither statement ranks MARL against all deterministic designs or
transfers the comparator's fresh-bank result to the learned policies.

The source factorial adds an attribution boundary. No registered contrast
established the positive 10\% effect after multiplicity control, but this does
not show zero effect, equivalence, or source irrelevance. The $N/P$ replacement
also changes a same-time algorithm input distribution and cannot isolate pure
semantic neighbour information.

claim.text:
Post-hoc frozen-path diagnostics are consistent with high recorded command
activity but do not identify its cause. For the common-reset componentwise
projector, executed-command TV plus terminal tracking residual is structurally
no greater than raw-command TV. Replacing the two previous-executed-command
actor inputs by their full-record means left 0.0710--0.2046 of raw TV in 48/48
tested channel-policy cases; the anchor is acausal. On a 24-policy by
four-profile grid, the constant-anchor/actual raw-RMS ratio had median 0.9588,
with 141/192 ratios at least 0.90, while temporal variation still contributed
37.45\%--51.23\% of raw RMS-squared energy for the included checkpoint. These
are recorded-path sensitivity and recurrence observations, not evidence that a
feedback loop, projector, reward term, or quasi-static mechanism caused the
R485 outcome.

claim.text:
The scope is one modified Kundur topology, four outcome-visible benchmark
profiles, six signed scenarios, one controller family, 26 seeds, and a fixed
budget. Learned policies were not evaluated on the separate fresh bank. The
6-s and 30-s results share traces and are not replications. All 208 training
manifests recorded the entropy coefficient at its lower bound at the final
checkpoint; without a registered convergence criterion this is a limitation,
not proof of convergence or divergence. Synchronous idealized communication
excludes delay, loss, and quantization.

Finally, comparator-relative command RMS and TV do not establish actuator
energy, wear, fatigue, thermal stress, absolute hardware limits, physical
safety, or deployment harm. The study supplies no probability of learner
failure, topology generalization, stability certificate, EMT or HIL validation,
or deployment claim. Each would require a separate prospective design rather
than reinterpretation of the sealed traces.

claim.text:
Existing work leaves three evaluation limitations relevant to that question.
First, model-based consensus, frequency-restoration, and mutual-damping
controllers explicitly coordinate paralleled VSGs~\cite{liu2020consensus,
shi2021restoration,fu2022mutual}, while reinforcement-learning studies adapt
inertia--droop or inertia--damping parameters to improve frequency or power
responses~\cite{yang2023ddic,lu2024sac,zhang2024maddpg,
benhmidouch2024rlvsg,kang2025madrl}; those controller-specific performance
results do not by themselves answer whether an adaptive policy satisfies a
common profile-complete endpoint-plus-command contract. Second, the cited
studies use controller-specific models and evaluation contracts; their
numerical results are therefore not treated as semantically interchangeable
with the benchmark object tested here. Third,
attribution validity is threatened both by training-run uncertainty that point
estimates can conceal~\cite{agarwal2021statistical} and by nominal source
comparisons in which actor inputs, critic inputs, and reward access change
together. A qualification study therefore needs a corrected common object,
explicit guard semantics, and paired-seed source interventions rather than a
success-style endpoint comparison.

detail: Existence and bibliographic metadata were checked against the linked publisher or official record; the title anchor matches the session-held metadata.

excerpt.text: Hybrid Symbolic-Numeric Framework for Power System Modeling and Analysis

claim.text:
The learner comprises four independent per-VSG soft actor--critic
agents~\cite{haarnoja2018sac}. Each agent uses a seven-component canonical physical
observation: local active power, local frequency and RoCoF, and the frequency
and RoCoF of its two ring neighbours. Appending the previously executed
two-component command gives a nine-dimensional Markov state. A Gaussian--tanh
actor and twin-Q critic each use four 128-unit ReLU hidden layers. Adam has
learning rate $3\times10^{-4}$; $\gamma=0.99$, target rate $\tau=0.005$,
replay capacity 10,000, batch size 256, target entropy $-2$, entropy coefficient
bounds $[0.005,5]$, and gradient-norm clipping at one. Training is stochastic;
evaluation uses the deterministic actor mean.

All six learner frequency/RoCoF slots use one canonical $60/50$ transform.
Actor, critic, replay, reward, and evaluation consume the transformed rows; no
path applies it twice. Authentic source $N$ preserves the same-time neighbour
tuple. Placebo source $P$ preserves recipient-local slots but takes the four
neighbour slots from row $\pi(i)=(i+1)\bmod4$. The $N/P$ contrast is therefore
a total input-source intervention, not an isolated semantic-information
intervention.

excerpt.text: Soft Actor-Critic: Off-Policy Maximum Entropy Deep Reinforcement Learning With a Stochastic Actor

claim.text:
Let $y_{acrps}=\log L_{acrps}$, where $L$ is the positive final-checkpoint
$J_d$ for actor source $a$, critic source $c$, reward access $r$, profile $p$,
and seed $s$. Equal-weight averaging over nuisance indices gives the four
registered within-seed contrasts
\begin{align}
d_s^A&=\langle y_{Pcrps}-y_{Ncrps}\rangle_{c,r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^C&=\langle y_{aPrps}-y_{aNrps}\rangle_{a,r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^{AC}&=\langle y_{PNrps}-y_{NNrps}-y_{PPrps}+y_{NPrps}\rangle_{r,p},\nonumber\\
d_s^{CR}&=\langle y_{aP1ps}-y_{aN1ps}-y_{aP0ps}+y_{aN0ps}\rangle_{a,p}.
\label{eq:contrasts}
\end{align}
Positive main effects indicate lower loss with authentic $N$; interaction signs
retain the registered ratio-of-ratios meaning. The 26 seeds, not profiles or
trajectories, are inference units. Exact one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests
compare each Hodges--Lehmann location to $\log(1.10)$, with one Holm family of
four~\cite{holm1979simple}. Non-rejection is neither zero effect nor
equivalence.

The formal inventory verifies 1,082/1,082 terminal artifacts and
5,088/5,088 trajectories, with no missing, duplicate, hash-invalid, or
parse-invalid item. All 848 6-s summaries are derived prefixes; no
available-case analysis or horizon pooling was performed.
